title: Trust Region Masking for Long-Horizon LLM Reinforcement Learning
claim: Token-level clipping fails to control sequence-level divergence, so training-inference mismatch grows and task performance degrades versus plain importance sampling.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared legend below, green vs orange curves
description: Two line charts sit side by side with a shared legend beneath them. The left plot shows the training-rollout log absolute perplexity gap against training step (0 to about 900). The green Token IS curve drops quickly and stays low, around 0.0005 to 0.0007. The orange PPO Clipping curve (0.8, 1.28) dips, then climbs back and fluctuates noisily around 0.0012 to 0.0017. The right plot shows AIME25 score against training step. Green rises steadily to about 0.26. Orange peaks near 0.19 at about step 130, then declines and plateaus near 0.15. Both plots have light grids, black frames, and large axis labels. The eye goes first to the gap between the green and orange curves.
caption: Token-level IS vs.\ PPO Clipping. Clipping exacerbates instability (larger PPL Gap, degraded score), confirming that token-level interventions cannot control $\Dkltokmax$.
abstract: Policy gradient methods for Large Language Models optimize a policy $Ï_Î¸$ via a surrogate objective computed from samples of a rollout policy $Ï_{\text{roll}}$. However, modern LLM-RL pipelines suffer from unavoidable implementation divergences -- backend discrepancies, Mixture-of-Experts routing discontinuities, and distributed training staleness -- causing off-policy mismatch ($Ï_{\text{roll}} \neq Ï_Î¸$) and approximation errors between the surrogate and the true objective. We demonstrate that classical trust region bounds on this error scale as $O(T^2)$ with sequence length $T$, rendering them vacuous for long-horizon tasks. To address this, we derive a family of bounds -- both KL-based and TV-based -- including a Pinsker-Marginal bound ($O(T^{3/2})$), a Mixed bound ($O(T)$), and an Adaptive bound that strictly generalizes the Pinsker-Marginal bound via per-position importance-ratio decomposition. Taking the minimum over all bounds yields the tightest known guarantee across all divergence regimes. Crucially, all bounds depend on the maximum token-level divergence $D_{\mathrm{KL}}^{\mathrm{tok,max}}$ (or $D_{\mathrm{TV}}^{\mathrm{tok,max}}$), a sequence-level quantity that cannot be controlled by token-independent methods like PPO clipping. We propose Trust Region Masking (TRM), which masks entire sequences violating the trust region, enabling the first non-vacuous monotonic improvement guarantees for long-horizon LLM-RL.
